7026-children-s-edition-of-touching-inci:
S B Shaw compiles a children's edition of touching incidents and remarkable answers to prayer, with pictures made specially for the work. The first preface says pictures will suggest thoughts of God and heaven and awaken desires to live pure lives, sooner or later leading many young readers to salvation. Shaw blesses all readers and promises stories sure to interest children and most older people too.

The lessons chosen stress kindness, sympathy, obedience, gratitude, courage, and faithfulness, with two further lessons the editor prizes. Children, he insists, can and should be true Christians, with sins forgiven for Jesus sake and hearts changed. The book is a Sunday school gift of short true tales and pictures for young hearts.
children-s-edition-of-touching-incidents:
S. B. Shaw's Children's Edition of Touching Incidents and Remarkable Answers to Prayer collects true stories for young readers, with pictures made specially for the work. Shaw says the pictures will turn young minds toward God and heaven and stir wishes for pure living.

The stories teach kindness, sympathy, obedience, gratitude, courage and faithfulness. Two further lessons stand above all: children can be true Christians, and one must be a Christian to be prepared for life and for death alike. Shaw addresses children directly, with confidence that older people will enjoy the stories too. Families seeking Victorian devotional reading for children will find this volume earnest and tender.
doe-osti-3030826-geologic-seawater-air-c:
Diana Acero Allard, Estefanny Davalos-Elizondo, Hyunjun Oh, and colleagues at the National Laboratory of the Rockies weigh a cool idea in report NLR/TP-5700-98308, dated April 2026. Puerto Rico heat and humidity keep air conditioners running hard, straining an old, fuel-dependent grid. GeoSWAC, short for Geologic Seawater Air Conditioning, would chill buildings with cold seawater drawn through local geology instead of power-hungry compressors. The study checks resources and costs around the San Juan metro area.

Geologic cross sections map heat flow under the city, crossing the University of Puerto Rico Rio Piedras campus. One key well, test hole NC-3, drilled in 1986, reached 375 feet. It passed through surface deposits and the Cibao Formation, a mixed stack of packstone, claystone, and sandstone, into old volcanic basement rock.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AgentOswaldFBIJ: FBI releases on Lee Harvey Oswald and the Kennedy assassination make up this file set, gathered under a researcher's filing title in the archive. The FBI's Oswald files run to thousands of pages: reports on his defection to the Soviet Union, his return, his Cuban activities, and the investigation after November 22, 1963. Sets like this one collect the Bureau's releases as they came out, piece by piece. The file is kept as issued, for readers working through the Bureau's paper trail.
nasa-tm-19710015944-voltage-transients-d:
Richard C Bainbridge and James Nestor of the Lewis Research Center wrote this May 1971 memorandum, NASA TM X-2291. It explains voltage spikes in the speed control circuit of a Brayton cycle alternator. The circuit switched power by phase angle, chopping the waveform. Each fast switch could jolt the output voltage. The team needed the cause before flight use.

They simulated the alternator, control circuit, and spare load on an analog computer. The simulation pinned the spikes on the alternator's own self inductance. Rapidly switching currents fought that inductance and kicked the voltage. A line filter already in the design proved effective. It kept the spikes away from the output terminals.
podcast-joerogan-sp6JkY3d0sw:
Hamilton Morris, a chemist and journalist, talks drugs with Joe Rogan in episode 177 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Morris later hosted Hamilton's Pharmacopeia, a TV series visiting drug cultures around the world. Even in this early talk, his mix of lab knowledge and field stories stands out.

Morris explains what key drugs actually do in the brain and body, in plain language. He shares tales from chemists, users, and makers he had met while reporting. Rogan, a veteran of drug talk, compares notes and stories. The episode blends hard science with the human stories that surround these molecules.
